newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil B Band to raise twice base price -- paper.
newsitem.headline: Brazil B Band to raise twice base price -- paper.

text.p: The Brazilian government will take in nearly double its asking price for 10 B Band cellular telephone concessions it put to tender last week, local daily O Estado de Sao Paulo said.

O Estado, quoting unnamed sources at consortia bidding on the concessions, said Brasilia has received offers more than 100 percent above the base price for Sao Paulo city and three other choice concession areas.
The paper said the areas, including Parana-Santa Catarina, Rio de Janeiro-Espirito Santo and Sao Paulo state, are in theory those where consortia foresee a quick return on investment.
O Estado did not give a dollar figure on how much the government could rake in.
The government set a total 3.78 billion real ($3.57 billion) base price for licensing fees for the 10 B Band areas.
Among them were minimum prices of 660 million reais each for Sao Paulo city and state, 500 million reais for Rio-Espirito Santo and 200 million reais for sparsely populated rural areas.
Government officials have said they hope to garner at least $5 billion, and market sources believe the Sao Paulo city concession alone will fetch at least $1 billion.
Fifteen consortia, comprised of foreign and local firms, bid last week on nine of 10 concession areas offered by the government.
No bids were cast for the area comprising the remote northern states of Amazonas, Amapa, Maranhao, Para and Roraima.
